steps.thought: I will list all available tests on the station to understand what diagnostic tools can be used to check the subsystems.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check all communication buses and subsystem enumeration.
steps.observation: The initial power_on_selftest passed successfully with all CAN nodes, UART devices, camera sensor, and I2C devices discovered correctly, indicating no catastrophic boot or bus enumeration failures.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power-on self-test passed cleanly, though all other subsystems still need to be tested.
Too early in the test flow to determine if a subtle performance or sensor fault is present.

steps.thought: I will run battery_rest_check to check the battery cell health at rest before proceeding to other subsystems.
steps.observation: The battery rest check passed successfully, showing nominal cell voltages around 4.15V and very low imbalance, ruling out dead or weak battery cells at rest.

hypotheses.rationale: Both power-on selftest and battery rest check passed with no failures, though further subsystem testing is required.
Only basic system and battery rest checks have been completed; other subsystems like ESCs, motors, IMU, compass, and camera remain untested.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test to check for any ESC commutation issues or sync errors across the ESCs as the next logical subsystem test.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test failed due to high sync errors (45) on esc_1, while all other ESCs showed normal telemetry. This points specifically to an ESC commutation desync issue on esc_1.

hypotheses.rationale: esc_1 reported 45 sync errors, well above the threshold of 5, while escs 2, 3, and 4 had normal sync error counts.
Other subsystems have not yet been tested, so secondary faults cannot be completely ruled out.

steps.thought: I need to run the motor_spin_test to see if esc_1 sync errors translate into actual motor performance issues or if reflash_esc_firmware is directly required.
steps.observation: The motor_spin_test and esc_telemetry tests show that motor_1 and esc_1 have severe issues, with motor_1 running at a low RPM (4938) with massive jitter (1096) and esc_1 reporting 45 sync errors. This confirms an issue on the esc_1/motor_1 subsystem.

hypotheses.rationale: High sync errors on esc_1 directly indicate commutation desync issues on that controller.
Low RPM and high RPM jitter on motor_1 could potentially be caused by a partial winding short or phase issue.

steps.thought: I will search the failure library for similar cases of ESC sync errors and motor RPM jitter on motor_1 to distinguish between an ESC commutation desync and a motor winding short.

args.query: esc_1 sync errors and motor_1 low rpm rpm jitter

matches.title: Motor stutters and loses sync
matches.symptom_summary: One motor stutters during spin up, rpm is low and unstable with very large rpm jitter. ESC telemetry on that channel shows many sync errors while back-EMF is detected. Packet loss is normal on all ESCs.
matches.root_cause: ESC commutation timing set wrong in firmware, causing desync on that channel.
matches.rework_notes: Reflash the ESC on the affected channel with the released firmware and timing profile.

matches.title: Motor will not spin, ESC sees no back-EMF
matches.symptom_summary: Spin test shows one motor at zero rpm drawing almost no current and staying at room temperature. ESC telemetry for that channel reports back-EMF not detected and zero sync errors. Other three motors normal.
matches.root_cause: Open stator winding (broken magnet wire at the solder cup).
matches.rework_notes: Replace the motor at the dead position. Check the phase wire solder joints on the replacement.

matches.title: ESC overheats and derates under sustained load
matches.symptom_summary: One ESC temperature climbs above 80 C during long runs and the motor rpm drops as the ESC derates. Sync errors low, packet loss normal.
matches.root_cause: Missing thermal pad between ESC FETs and the heatsink.
matches.rework_notes: Install the thermal pad. ESC temperature is the tell.

steps.observation: The search failure library match FL-004 exactly mirrors our symptoms of high sync errors on esc_1 and huge RPM jitter with low RPM on motor_1, pointing to ESC_DESYNC.

hypotheses.rationale: High sync errors on esc_1 and severe RPM jitter/low RPM on motor_1 match historical records for ESC commutation desync.
Low RPM and high jitter could theoretically stem from a winding issue, but telemetry sync errors make ESC desync far more likely.

steps.thought: The failure library match FL-004 and telemetry data conclusively point to an ESC commutation desync on esc_1, so we are ready to propose the rework action.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
